newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet tightens rules on pension premiums.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet tightens rules on pension premiums.

text.p: Poland's government on Tuesday approved a regulation on contributions to the state-controlled pension system, which the business community said amounts to increasing the already high premiums.

Under the new rules, the size of obligatory premiums to the Social Security Office (ZUS) would depend not only on on workers' bare wages but also on other extra-income, Labour Minister Tadeusz Zielinski told a news briefing.
Under the rules effective so far, employers had to contribute to ZUS 45 percent of their employees' salaries.
They will now have to contribute also 45 percent on what they pay for overtime work, special bonuses and some other allowances.

Many employers, who had complained pension premiums were already too high and pushed labour costs beyond acceptable levels, said the regulation amounted to the premium rise under the inefficient system, reform of which have been dragging for years.
"The business community sees this regulation as a veiled increase of the premium," said Jeremi Mordasewicz, a deputy head of the Business Centre Club, an employers' group.
Zielinski said the new rules were necessary to prevent many companies from evading paying required premium.
Many firms book a substantial part of their workers earnings as extra benefits even though they should be embraced by the salary, he said. The procedure is used to pay less to ZUS, he added.
